mainTopic: Learning חזקה from שור המועד, its limits, and the search for the חכמים' source for three years
overview: The גמרא is exploring the idea that the three years of חזקה are learned from שור המועד: three gorings make an ox 'established', and three years of use make someone the established owner of land. It explains why the ox's fourth goring does not spoil the comparison. It then defends the comparison against two challenges: why a חזקה needs a claim, and why a מחאה counts even when the holder is not present. Next it tests the comparison on timing. Following רבי מאיר, three gorings in one day are enough, so the גמרא asks about fig fruits, caper fruits, and alfalfa cut quickly. The answer is that each harvest must be a truly separate, normal crop. When alfalfa is properly harvested three times in three months, the גמרא admits this would be a חזקה, because the ox derivation follows רבי ישמעאל, who counts harvests rather than years. It then asks what the source is for the חכמים, who require three full years. רב יוסף brings a פסוק from ירמיהו about writing deeds, but אביי rejects it as mere good advice.

steps.title: Why the ox's fourth goring does not break the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to שור המועד is completed: three gorings match three years, and the extra goring is only needed because there is nothing to pay until the ox gores again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other goring, the fourth, is only needed because before the ox gores again, what is there to pay? But here, once he has used the land and eaten its produce for three years, the land stands established in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the idea that the three years of חזקה are learned from שור המועד. It explains why the ox seems to need a fourth goring while land needs only three years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three gorings make the ox a מועד, and that matches three years of using the land. The owner only pays full damages for a fourth goring, but that is not because the status is incomplete. It is simply because until the ox gores again, there is no damage to pay for. With land, nothing else needs to happen: after three years the holder is already established.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that has gored three times and is now 'established' as a goring ox; its owner pays full damages
And the other one (here: the fourth goring)
Gored
In his possession / domain

phrases.english: And the other one,
phrases.notes: He means the fourth goring. Three gorings make the ox a מועד, and full payment only comes when it gores again.

phrases.english: when it has not gored, what is there to pay?
Here, since he has eaten from it for three years,
it stands in his possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, כִּי לָא נְגַח – מַאי לְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this amud: why does the ox need a fourth goring while land needs only three years? The answer keeps the derivation of חזקה from שור המועד in place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three years of use on land matches three gorings of the ox. The fourth goring is needed only for there to be something to pay, so land needs nothing beyond three years.

steps.title: Then why must a חזקה come with a claim?
steps.stepSummary: If חזקה works automatically like the ox's status, possession without any claim should also be a חזקה. But a משנה says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, possession that has no claim with it should also count as a חזקה! Why then did we learn in a משנה: Any possession that has no claim with it is not a חזקה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison to the ox. An ox becomes מועד automatically, yet the משנה says a חזקה on land only works if the holder claims he got the land in a valid way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox does not need any 'explanation' to become a מועד, since three gorings are enough. If land works the same way, three years alone should be enough. But the משנה says that without a טענה, such as 'I bought it', there is no חזקה. This seems to show that חזקה is not like the ox after all.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (opens a challenge that follows from what was just said)
Established possession; here, using land for three years so it is presumed yours
A claim, such as 'I bought it' or 'it was given to me'

phrases.english: But if so,
possession that has no claim with it
should be a valid possession!
Why did we learn:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in this פרק (דף מא).

phrases.english: Any possession that has no claim with it
is not a valid possession?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, חֲזָקָה שֶׁאֵין עִמָּהּ טַעֲנָה תֶּיהְוֵי חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison to שור המועד that was just completed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of חזקה from שור המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ox's status comes automatically from the three gorings with no claim needed. So if land is learned from the ox, three years should work even without a claim, which goes against the משנה.

steps.title: The claim is needed because we do not argue for him
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a חזקה needs a claim is not about how חזקה works. It is because the court will not make up a claim the holder himself does not make.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason a חזקה needs a claim? Because a חזקה works since we say: perhaps it really is as he says, that he bought it. Now that he himself does not claim this, should we claim it for him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Three years really do create a presumption, but that presumption only supports something the holder actually claims.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה protects the holder because we think, 'maybe he really bought it, like he says.' If he never says he bought it, there is nothing for the חזקה to support. The court will not invent a claim for him. So the משנה's rule does not show that חזקה is different from the ox, and the comparison stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Perhaps it is as he says
Claims / argues
Should we claim for him?

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the three years are worthless without a claim. It says the presumption exists, but the court only uses it to back up what the holder himself argues.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because we say: perhaps it is as he says,
phrases.notes: In a normal case the holder says he bought the land, and the three years make us believe him.

phrases.english: now that he himself does not claim,
should we claim for him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה about possession without a claim.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind the משנה so that it does not conflict with the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Requiring a claim means that three years alone do not create the presumption, unlike the ox.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three years do create the presumption. The claim is needed only because the court will not argue on the holder's behalf what he himself does not argue.

steps.title: רב עוירא: then a protest not in his presence should not count
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא challenges the comparison to the ox: testimony about a שור המועד must be given in the owner's presence, so a מחאה against a holder should also have to be made in his presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא challenged this: But if so, a protest made not in his presence should not be a protest, just like a שור המועד. Just as for a שור המועד we require that it be in his presence, so too here we should require that it be in his presence!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא raises a new challenge to learning חזקה from the ox. He points to a rule about the ox that does not seem to match the הלכה about land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox becomes a מועד only if the warnings about its goring are given in front of its owner. If land is learned from the ox, then a מחאה, where the original owner protests that the holder is on his land, should also only work in front of the holder. But in practice a מחאה counts even when the holder is not there, so the comparison seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (a sharp objection)
A protest by the original owner that stops a חזקה from forming
Not in his presence
Similar to / like
We require

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge tests whether the details of שור המועד really carry over to חזקה, and it sets up the גמרא's next discussion.

phrases.english: Rav Avira challenged it:
But if so, a protest not in his presence
should not be a protest,
just like a forewarned ox;
just as with a forewarned ox we require it in his presence,
phrases.notes: The witnesses about the goring have to testify in front of the ox's owner.

phrases.english: so too here we should also require it in his presence!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב עַוִּירָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, מֶחָאָה שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו לָא תֶּיהְוֵי מֶחָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new challenge is made against the same comparison to the ox.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of חזקה from שור המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If land follows the ox, every rule should carry over. Testimony about the ox must be in the owner's presence, so a מחאה should only work in the holder's presence, but a מחאה counts even when he is not there.

steps.title: Why a protest does not need to be made in front of the holder
steps.stepSummary: An ox's warning must be given before the owner because the תורה says so. A מחאה reaches the holder anyway, because word spreads from friend to friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, by the ox, the פסוק says 'and warning was given to its owner.' Here, your friend has a friend, and your friend's friend has a friend, so the news will reach him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב עוירא's challenge. It explains why a מחאה can be made even when the holder is not there, unlike testimony about a שור המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the ox's owner must be present comes from a special word in the פסוק, 'בבעליו'. It is not a general logical rule. With a מחאה, all that matters is that the holder finds out, and news spreads from person to person until it reaches him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And warning was given to its owner' (the פסוק about a שור המועד)
Your friend has a friend, meaning news always spreads
A formal protest by the owner against the person living on his land

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why a מחאה counts even when the holder is not there. What matters is that word of it will reach him.

phrases.english: There, "and warning has been given to its owner" is written;
phrases.notes: שמות 21:29. The word בבעליו is read as 'in front of its owner.'

phrases.english: here, your friend has a friend,
and the friend of your friend has a friend.
phrases.notes: Whoever hears the protest will tell someone, and eventually the holder hears about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עוירא's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases. The ox's rule comes from a special פסוק, while for a מחאה it is enough that the news spreads.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חזקה is modeled on שור המועד, a מחאה would also need to be made in the holder's presence.
steps.terutzMaskana: The presence rule is a special decree for the ox only. A מחאה works as long as the holder can find out about it.

steps.title: Should eating three fruits in one day count as a חזקה?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, an ox becomes מועד even with three gorings in one day. So eating three fruits from a fig tree in one day should also make a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says that if an ox spaced out its gorings, the owner is liable, and if it gored close together, then all the more so. So if someone ate three fruits in one day, for example from a fig tree, that should be a חזקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the ox comparison further. Following רבי מאיר, gorings close together still count, so three quick harvests should count too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If three gorings on the same day are enough for רבי מאיר, then time does not seem to matter for the ox. If חזקה really matches the ox, eating three fruits in a single day should be enough, and three years would not be needed. That would be a strange result.

keyTerms.meaning: It spaced out its gorings (on separate days)
It gored close together (on the same day)
All the more so
A fig tree

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir, who says:
if it spaced out its gorings, the owner is liable,
if it gored close together, all the more so;
if he ate three fruits in one day,
for example, of a fig tree, let it be a presumption of ownership!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר רִיחֵק נְגִיחוֹתָיו חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the ox comparison, this time about timing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between three years of חזקה and the three gorings of a שור המועד (step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי מאיר, the three gorings can all happen on one day. So three harvests on one day should also be enough for a חזקה.

steps.title: Each harvest must be a separate event, like separate gorings
steps.stepSummary: Each goring happens on its own, after the one before it is over. In the same way, each harvest of fruit must be a separate event, and fruits that are all on the tree at once do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be like a שור המועד. With a שור המועד, when this goring is happening, that goring does not exist. Here too, it must be that when this fruit exists, that fruit does not exist yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison is not about how many days pass. It is about each act being a separate event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three gorings are always three separate events, even on one day. Three fruits taken from one fig tree that were all hanging there together are really just one harvest. So the comparison to the ox requires three separate crops, not just three acts of eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, modeled on
At the time when
A goring

phrases.english: It is similar to a forewarned ox:
just as with a forewarned ox,
at the time when it has this goring,
that goring does not exist,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי בְּעִידָּנָא דְּאִיתָא לְהַאי פֵּירָא
phrases.english: here too, at the time when this fruit exists,
that fruit must not exist.
phrases.notes: In other words, the second crop must not be there yet while the first one is on the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי מאיר in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies what the comparison is really about: separate events, not the passing of time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three acts of eating on one day would match three gorings on one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each act must be separate. Fruits that are all on the tree at once count as one crop.

steps.title: What about a caper bush whose fruits ripen on different days?
steps.stepSummary: A צלף ripens its fruits one day after another. So three fruits eaten on three days should be separate events and count as a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate three fruits in three days, for example from a caper bush, that should be a חזקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new rule. With a צלף, each fruit ripens on a different day, so the fruits seem to be separate, just like gorings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said a new 'event' happens when one fruit is ready only after the earlier one is gone. With a caper bush, a new fruit becomes ready each day. That seems to meet the rule, and it would allow a חזקה in only three days.

keyTerms.meaning: A caper bush, whose fruits ripen one after another
Three days

phrases.english: If he ate three fruits in three days,
for example, of a caper bush, let it be a presumption of ownership!
phrases.notes: A caper bush's fruits ripen one at a time, day after day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכְלַהּ תְּלָתָא פֵּרֵי בִּתְלָתָא יוֹמֵי כְּגוֹן צָלָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 7 that each fruit must be a separate event.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Caper fruits ripen separately, one each day. So they should count as three separate events within three days.

steps.title: Caper fruits were already there, just finishing to ripen
steps.stepSummary: The caper fruits were all already on the bush. They were just finishing their ripening, so they are not truly separate events.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the fruit is at least already there, and it is just finishing its ripening over time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the caper's fruits do not count as separate. They all existed together and only finished ripening on different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separate means that the next fruit did not exist at all yet. Caper fruits are all on the bush at once, even if each one ripens on a different day. So they are one crop, not three separate events like gorings.

keyTerms.meaning: At least, in any case
It is gradually finishing (its ripening)

steps.whatToRemember: The ox comparison teaches that a חזקה needs three truly separate acts of use. Fruits that are all on the tree at the same time, even if they ripen on different days, count as one crop.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that three different days is enough. What counts is whether the fruit existed at all before, not when it became ripe.

phrases.english: There, the fruit at least is already there,
and it is just gradually finishing its ripening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the caper challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case more sharply: fruit that already exists and is still ripening is not a new, separate fruit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Caper fruits that ripen on different days would count as three separate events.
steps.terutzMaskana: The caper fruits all existed together. Only their ripening was spread out, so they count as one crop.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only truly separate crops count toward a חזקה under the ox comparison.

steps.title: Alfalfa eaten three times in thirty days
steps.stepSummary: Alfalfa grows back fast. If someone cut and ate it three times in thirty days, that should be three separate harvests and make a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate three crops in thirty days, such as alfalfa, it should count as a חזקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the 'separate events' rule from step 7 further. It brings a crop that truly grows back after each cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 and 9 said fruits already on the plant at once do not count. Alfalfa really regrows after it is cut, so each cutting is new growth. So by that rule, three cuttings in a month should make a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Alfalfa, a plant that grows back quickly after it is cut
Fruits or crops, meaning harvests
A presumption of ownership that comes from using a field
Thirty days

phrases.english: If he ate three crops from it in thirty days
such as alfalfa,
phrases.notes: Alfalfa grows back after each cutting, so you can harvest it again and again in a short time.

phrases.english: let it be a חזקה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכְלַהּ תְּלָתָא פֵּירֵי בִּתְלָתִין יוֹמֵי כְּגוֹן אַסְפַּסְתָּא לֶיהֱוֵי חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new test case on the 'separate events' rule from steps 7 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that three separate harvests, like three separate gorings, make a חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Alfalfa truly regrows, so three cuttings are three separate events, even within thirty days. That should be enough by the rule.

steps.title: Cutting it barely grown is snatching, not farming
steps.stepSummary: Three cuttings in thirty days means he cut it each time when it had barely grown. That is snatching, not normal use of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? It sprouts a little and he eats it, sprouts a little and he eats it. There he is just snatching and eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that three alfalfa harvests in a month can only happen if he cuts it too early each time. That does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה comes from using the land the normal way an owner would. Cutting tiny shoots over and over is grabbing, not real farming. So these cuttings do not count as harvests.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look in practice?
Sprouts a little, just begins to grow
Snatching, grabbing early
He snatches and eats

phrases.english: What is the case?
Where it sprouts a little and he eats it,
sprouts a little and he eats it;
there, it is snatching
that he is snatching and eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי דְּקָדַיח וְאָכְלָה דְּקָדַיח וְאָכְלָה הָתָם מִשְׁמָט הוּא דְּקָא שָׁמֵיט וְאָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the alfalfa challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: such quick harvests are not normal use of the land.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any regrowth counts as a separate harvest, so three cuttings in thirty days should make a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only normal, full harvests count. Snatching barely grown alfalfa is not normal use, so it does not make a חזקה.

steps.title: Alfalfa harvested properly three times in three months
steps.stepSummary: If the alfalfa grew fully and was harvested normally three times in three months, that should make a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate three crops in three months, such as alfalfa, it should count as a חזקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the gap left by step 11. Now each harvest is full and normal, just spread over three months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 rejected only early snatching. Over three months, each cutting is a full, normal harvest and a separate event. So it seems three months should be enough for a חזקה, not three years.

keyTerms.meaning: Three months

phrases.english: If he ate three crops from it in three months
such as alfalfa,
let it be a חזקה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכְלַהּ תְּלָתָא פֵּירֵי בִּתְלָתָא יַרְחֵי כְּגוֹן אַסְפַּסְתָּא לֶיהֱוֵי חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the challenge so the answer of step 11 no longer works.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a חזקה needs three years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three normal, separate harvests happen within three months. If separate harvests are what count, three months should be enough.

steps.title: The teaching follows רבי ישמעאל, and yes, it counts
steps.stepSummary: The teaching of the הולכי אושא follows רבי ישמעאל. By his view, three such harvests really do make a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the travelers to אושא? רבי ישמעאל. According to רבי ישמעאל, it is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It says the derivation it has been building on follows רבי ישמעאל, and he agrees that three harvests are enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not reject the case. It says whose view this is. For רבי ישמעאל, the count is harvests, not years, so three proper alfalfa harvests in three months would make a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: The people traveling to the town of Usha, whose teaching is being discussed
Indeed so, yes, that is right

phrases.english: Who are the travelers to Usha?
It is רבי ישמעאל;
according to רבי ישמעאל, it is indeed so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן הוֹלְכֵי אוּשָׁא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by agreeing with it and naming the תנא whose view it fits.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the teaching follows a specific תנא who accepts the result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three harvests in three months cannot be a חזקה, since a חזקה needs three years.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ישמעאל, three harvests are what count, so it really is a חזקה.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying everyone agrees. It means only רבי ישמעאל holds this, which is why it asks about the חכמים in step 15.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: for רבי ישמעאל, three harvests equal three years
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes רבי ישמעאל: in a field of trees, three different harvests count as three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי ישמעאל says, when is this said? In a grain field. But in a field of trees, if he gathered his produce, picked his olives, and gathered his figs, these count as three years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה to prove that רבי ישמעאל counts harvests, not years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל says that in a tree field, three harvests of different crops, even in less time, count as three years. That shows he measures a חזקה by harvests. This supports step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? This limits an earlier rule.
A 'white field,' meaning a grain field with no trees
A field of trees
Summer fruit, figs

phrases.english: As we learned: רבי ישמעאל says:
When is this said?
In a grain field,
but in a field of trees,
if he gathered his produce,
and picked his olives,
and gathered his figs,
these count as three years.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בִּשְׂדֵה הַלָּבָן
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי ישמעאל counts a חזקה by harvests, not by years.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי ישמעאל says three harvests in a tree field count as three years.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל measures a חזקה by three separate harvests. That is why three proper alfalfa harvests would be enough for him.

steps.title: What do the חכמים hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים, who require three full years, explain the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what the source or reasoning is for the חכמים, who require three years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The derivation from the warned ox fits רבי ישמעאל's 'harvest' view. The חכמים count years, not harvests, so that derivation does not seem to fit them. The גמרא now needs their source.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים, the majority view, who require three years
What? What is their view or source?

phrases.english: According to the חכמים, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After placing the teaching with רבי ישמעאל, the גמרא turns to the other side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning for the חכמים, who require three full years for a חזקה.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from ירמיהו's warning
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers the question from step 15. He brings a פסוק in ירמיהו where the נביא tells people to write deeds for fields, because the land would be conquered before they could hold the field for three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A verse says, "Fields shall they buy with money, and write it in a deed and seal it." The prophet was standing in the tenth year and warning about the eleventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 15: where do the חכמים get the rule that a חזקה needs three full years? רב יוסף brings a source from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו spoke in the tenth year of צדקיהו, and the land would be conquered in the eleventh year. Someone buying a field then would have less than three years before exile, so living there could not build a חזקה. That is why the נביא told them to write deeds, and this shows that a חזקה needs three years.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse is written: introduces a proof from a פסוק
Writing it in a document: a deed of sale
And seal it: signing and sealing the deed
Prophet: here ירמיהו
Warns, cautions

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ירמיהו meant that buying a field needs a deed in general. The point is the timing: there was not enough time before the conquest to hold the field for three years.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A verse is written:
"Fields shall they buy with money,
and write it in a deed and seal it"
for the prophet was standing in the tenth year,
phrases.notes: This means the tenth year of King צדקיהו's reign.

phrases.english: and warning about the eleventh year.
phrases.notes: The eleventh year is when the land would be conquered, so a buyer would have less than three years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by giving the חכמים a scriptural source for the three-year rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three-year rule is learned from ירמיהו telling people to write deeds, since less than three years remained before the conquest and a חזקה could not be built.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a חזקה requires three full years.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 32:44, said in the tenth year with the conquest coming in the eleventh.

steps.title: אביי: maybe it was just good advice
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof. Perhaps ירמיהו was only giving sensible advice to write deeds, not teaching that a חזקה needs three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Perhaps there the prophet is just teaching us good advice!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away רב יוסף's proof from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed the deed was needed because a חזקה could not be built in time. אביי says the פסוק does not prove that. Writing a deed is simply smart, because it saves the need for witnesses about how long he lived on the land. So the פסוק says nothing about how many years a חזקה takes.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps: opens a different way to read the source
There: in that case, the פסוק
Good advice: practical wisdom, not a law
He is teaching us

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes רב יוסף's source, so the גמרא still needs another source for the three-year rule of the חכמים.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps there
he is teaching us good advice!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דִּלְמָא הָתָם עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רב יוסף's proof from the פסוק. It does not reject the three-year rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק can be read as practical advice to write deeds, so it does not show that a חזקה is impossible in less than three years.
